text:
julie: Strange TypeScript behavior in Edge ESM bundles: generic overloads are losing inference and falling back to `any` when consumed from Cloudflare/Vercel edge. Works fine in Node.

rafi: Can you show the exported signatures and your package.json exports/types config? those usually bite here.

julie: Minimal SDK type: 
```ts
export function exec<T>(opts: { payload: T }): Promise<Response<T>>;
export function exec(opts: { payload: unknown }): Promise<Response<any>>;
```
Importing in worker: `sdk.exec({ payload: { name: 'x' } })` — editor shows payload as any, no autocomplete.

kevin: Are you bundling before deploy? esbuild sometimes rewrites import specifiers and the consumer ends up resolving the cjs d.ts in node_modules because package.json exports aren't honored by the bundler.

nina: Also check if your published package has both dist/cjs/index.d.ts and dist/esm/index.d.ts but "types" only points at the cjs one. Edge runtimes prefer the module field and may pick types differently.

julie: package.json: `"main": "dist/cjs/index.js", "module": "dist/esm/index.js", "types": "dist/cjs/index.d.ts", "exports": {"import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"}` — I thought types picks up automatically.

rafi: Types don't follow exports unless you add a types entry per export or use typesVersions. For modern TS consumers: add `"exports": {"import": {"types": "dist/esm/index.d.ts", "default": "dist/esm/index.js"}, "require": {"types": "dist/cjs/index.d.ts", "default": "dist/cjs/index.js"}}`. That helps TS resolve correct d.ts for import vs require.

kevin: Another angle: the overload + unknown fallback pattern can be ambiguous to the inference engine when TS resolves to a different .d.ts file that orders overloads differently. Flip the overload order? But better is a single generic signature with a fallback conditional type.

nina: Example rewrite that tends to be more resilient: 
```ts
export function exec<T = unknown>(opts: { payload: T & {} }): Promise<Response<T>>;
// or
type UnwrapInput<T> = unknown extends T ? any : T;
export function exec<T = unknown>(opts: { payload: UnwrapInput<T> }): Promise<Response<T>>;
```

julie: Hmm good. Also saw a weird case where tsc --declaration produced different d.ts on CI vs local because our build step used rollup + dts plugin on CI but local we run tsc. CI was publishing the rollup-generated d.ts which reordered overloads.

rafi: Yup. Ensure the published declarations come from a single source: prefer `tsc --emitDeclarationOnly --declaration --outDir dist/types` and point types there. Avoid re-generating types with rollup unless you validate the output.

kevin: For Edge consumers, set package exports with explicit types mapping and bump TS minimum to 4.7+ so moduleResolution=node16/node20 works predictably. Also consider `typesVersions` for older TS support.

nina: Quick repro steps: create toy package with both cjs/esm d.ts, then build a small Cloudflare worker that imports it (via Wrangler local) and inspect how the editor resolves types. Runs fast to catch the mismatch.

julie: Will do that. One more wrinkle: esbuild's externalization flag caused our worker bundle to import from the package root during the dev build, which made the editor resolve types from the uncompiled src folder (missing transforms).

rafi: Pro tip: add an index.d.ts at package root that re-exports the correct declarations (thin surface) so editors get a stable entry while runtime still uses exports mapping. That reduces surprise for IDEs.

kevin: Also document this in the SDK authoring guide: preferred pattern for generics + a checklist for package.json -> exports/types mapping and a CI job that verifies d.ts resolution from a Node/Esm/Edge consumer.

ci-bot: ci: types-check job started for branch/edge-typing-fix (matrix: node16,node20,bun,cloudflare).

julie: Thanks all, I'll open a small RFC with the proposed changes: explicit export types, single-generic refactor, and a d.ts publish pipeline. Will attach repro link.

nina: If you want, I can pair on the typesVersions map; I have a snippet we used at my last job.

julie: Sweet, assigning you and rafi. I'll paste the repro link shortly. :rocket:
